info.title: pannelAI API
info.summary: Management and data-plane API for the pannelAI gateway.
info.description: OpenAPI 3.1 contract for app-serv. Management routes use the pannel_session cookie. Data-plane routes use a gateway key when settings.security.require_api_key is enabled. Error envelopes are defined by the ManagementError and DataPlaneError schemas.

gatewayKey.description: Gateway key created through the management API.

ChatRequestMessage.description: One request turn. content may be omitted only for an assistant turn that carries tool_calls.

VideoJob.description: The async video job both video routes answer with, normalized across providers. Status is one of queued, in_progress, succeeded, or failed; an upstream state no mapping knows is passed through lower-cased rather than reported as a terminal one.

task_id.description: The id the poll route takes as its path segment.

url.description: The generated asset, present once the job succeeded.

b64_json.description: The generated asset inline, present when the upstream answered bytes rather than a URL (a Vertex generation without a storage URI).

progress.description: The upstream's own percentage, present when it reports one.

error.description: The upstream's own message, present once the job failed.

tags.description: The operator's labels on this row, in the canonical lowercase spelling a bulk selector matches against.

disabled_until.description: When an operator's park releases on its own. Absent means permanent, which is what a switch with no window is.

last_selected_at.description: When rotation last CHOSE this credential or account, distinct from when it last served a call (SPEC-API-001 7.5). Absent for one that has never been chosen.

last_error_class.description: Which failure the last refusal was classified as, in the router's own vocabulary (SPEC-API-001 7.5). Absent for a key that never failed or served since.

reset_source.description: How the wait on the parked key was arrived at. header is a Retry-After the vendor sent, body a reset the vendor stated in its own text, default a window the gateway chose. Absent for a key parked before classification existed.

signature_id.description: The recogniser that named this failure, so an operator can tell a park the vendor warranted from one the gateway guessed. Absent when no signature claimed it.

tags.description: The operator's labels on this row, in the canonical lowercase spelling a bulk selector matches against.

disabled_until.description: When an operator's park releases on its own. Absent means permanent, which is what a switch with no window is.

last_selected_at.description: When rotation last CHOSE this credential or account, distinct from when it last served a call (SPEC-API-001 7.5). Absent for one that has never been chosen.

auth_hint.description: The registry's credential-format sentence (draft 036 slice B), served verbatim, and it names the upstream URL where the operator mints the credential. Absent when the provider declares none.

thinking_levels.description: Union of the levels this provider's models accept, registry models and custom rows alike (SPEC-API-001 §7.14). Absent when no model reasons.

source.description: Where the list came from, "upstream" or "registry".

warning.description: Why the list is not from the upstream, when it is not.

model_id.description: The model string a client would send, without the provider prefix.

limit.description: Models to probe. Absent asks for the default budget; a larger value is clamped to the ceiling, and the answer reports how many ran.

endpoint_id.description: The connection that answered, when the routing got that far.

status.description: The upstream's own HTTP code, present only when the failure carried one.

error_code.description: The data plane's machine code, or MODEL_TEST_TIMEOUT when the probe ran out of its budget. Present only on a failed row.

source.description: Where the tested list came from, "upstream" or "registry".

warning.description: Why the list is not from the upstream, when it is not.

tested.description: Rows returned. Less than total means the budget or the limit stopped it.

stopped.description: Set when the sweep ran out of budget before reaching every model.

QuotaWindowList.description: Paged over provider groups (docs/PORT/006-PORT-QUOTA-PAGING.md D1); per_page counts provider groups on this route, and one page carries every window of the page's groups.

published.description:
The provider's own answer for every account belonging to the provider
groups on this page, served from the cache the poll worker writes.
Account, not counted window, is the unit here: an endpoint that has
routed no traffic has no counted row and still gets a card, which is
why an entry may carry `never_polled`.
It rides on the collection because asking each provider during a page
read is one outbound call per account, the N+1 shape AGENTS.md §1.7
blocks here. Additive: a client reading only `data` sees exactly what
it saw before.

published_note.description:
Present only when the provider cache could not be read at all. The
counted windows are still true and still arrive, so the alternative
to naming the gap is a page of cards that look like accounts whose
providers published nothing.

truncated.description:
True when the row ceiling cut this page, so the rows below are not
everything the page's provider groups hold. Paging bounds the groups
per round trip, and a separate ceiling bounds the rows, which AGENTS.md
§1.7 requires of a screen read. Without the flag a cut page reads as
accounts that routed nothing, the same misstatement published_note
names. Either of the page's two reads can be cut; the page is
incomplete when either was.

QuotaEndpointDetail.description: The stored cap (null when none is set) plus every window for one endpoint.

PublishedQuotaWindowResponse.description:
One bucket the provider published about its own account. Amounts are
decimal strings at the precision the provider reported (SPEC-API-001 §4),
not the fixed eight-place scale the counted windows use, because a credit
balance of 3000 is not known to eight places. `total` is absent when the
provider states no ceiling, which is not a ceiling of zero.

total.description: Decimal string. Absent when the bucket is unbounded.

resets_at.description: When the bucket refills, or expires when it never refills.

unit.description:
The dimension the provider counts in, when it names one (`requests`,
`tokens`, `%`, or a currency code for a balance). Absent means a bare
counter, which is a fact rather than a missing value.

unlimited.description: The provider publishes no ceiling for this bucket, so there is no share to draw.

is_credit_balance.description:
A money balance rather than a capped window. Not a synonym for
`unlimited`: a prepaid wallet holds finite money and no periodic
ceiling, and rendering either as a percentage of a total the
provider never claimed would misstate it.

recurring.description: False marks a one-shot pack, whose `resets_at` is an expiry rather than a refill.

PublishedQuotaUsageResponse.description:
The provider's own answer about one connection. `message` carries the
soft outcome (the family publishes nothing, the credential was refused,
the provider errored) and is then the whole answer with `data` empty.

plan.description: The tier the provider names this account by, when it names one.

fetched_at.description:
When the provider said the FIGURES in `data`, not when this process
served them. It dates the numbers rather than the attempt: a soft
answer (a `message` with an empty `data`) is stored by the poll
scheduler without touching the numbers, so its instant remains the
one the row was created with (the zero time, which serializes as
0001-01-01T00:00:00Z) until a read that carried figures replaces
it. That placeholder is not a stamp and must not be printed as one.
Figures can also outlive the read that failed to refresh them, so
dating them by a later attempt would be wrong the other way.

cached.description:
True when this is the poll worker's stored answer rather than a read
taken at this instant. The flag travels with the figure because
`fetched_at` is when the provider said it, not when this process
served it, and a number whose age is unstated cannot be acted on.

failures.description:
How many consecutive polls of this account produced no answer. It is
reported because a card can hold figures and a failing poll at the same
instant: the worker keeps the last good numbers rather than wiping them,
so without this count the operator sees a figure with no sign that the
last attempt refused to replace it. The reference draws the same line by
letting some families fail loudly and others answer softly.

last_attempt_at.description:
When the worker last asked this account, successfully or not. Distinct
from `fetched_at`, which dates the figures: a failed poll moves this
instant and leaves the older stamp where the surviving numbers were said.

never_polled.description:
The account exists and is on this page, but the worker has not
answered for it yet. Absence of an answer is a different claim from
an answer of absence (a provider that published nothing says so in
`message`) and the card has to tell them apart. Such an entry
carries no numbers and no `fetched_at` worth printing.

UsageLiveActive.description: One request the gateway is routing right now.

combo.description: The model combo the client addressed, empty when the request addressed a single model. It travels beside model because the combo is what the client named and model is the member that answered.

UsageLiveFrame.description:
One `data:` payload of the live Usage stream. Full state rather than a delta, so a client that
missed a frame recovers on the next one. Both lists are always arrays, never null: an empty
in-flight set is a fact and `null` would be a second spelling of it.

active.description: The in-flight set, oldest first, so the longest-running request is the first row.

recent.description: The requests that just finished, newest first, bounded by the gateway.

error_provider.description: The provider the gateway last reported an error for, or an empty string.

fallback_strategy.description: The credential rotation default for every provider (SPEC-API-001 7.5).

provider_strategies.description: Per-provider overrides, keyed by provider id. Sent whole; an absent entry inherits the global default.

failure_classes.description: Per-class overrides the whole group inherits, keyed by class name. Sent whole; an absent class keeps the documented action and windows. A class that implicates no credential is refused, because the router reads no window for it.

FailureClassPolicyPatch.description: What one recognised failure class does (SPEC-API-001 7.5). Each field is optional on its own: an entry that names only the action leaves the ceiling and cooldown it inherits. A provider entry merges over the group, and the group over the documented default.

action.description: park withholds the credential for its rest and moves on, rotate moves on without withholding, stop ends the request on this failure because no other credential answers it differently.

ceiling_seconds.description: The longest rest a wait the gateway computed may produce, measured from the failure. A reset the vendor stated itself is only bounded by this, never shortened below what the vendor promised.

default_cooldown_seconds.description: The flat park used when neither a stated reset nor a Retry-After was found. Unset keeps the class's own ladder, which is how a rate limit still escalates.

KeyParkPatch.description: The key-parking budget in seconds (SPEC-API-001 §7.5). Each window is optional on its own: an unnamed one keeps the value it has, and a provider entry that names none inherits the group's. The ladder ceilings are not configurable.

auth_seconds.description: The first credential-shaped failure parks the key for this long, then doubles.

rate_limit_seconds.description: The first rate limit backs this long, then doubles.

transient_seconds.description: How long an upstream 5xx parks the key that served it. Flat.

billing_seconds.description: The first upstream 402 parks the account's key this long, then doubles up to six hours.

quota_seconds.description: How long this provider's allowance takes to come back. It caps the quota ladder and it is the window an operator's disable parks for, because a vendor that resets every five hours says the same thing about a manual park. Unset answers a day.

FailoverBudgetPatch.description: The bounds on one client request's credential walk (SPEC-API-001 §7.14). Each bound is optional on its own: widening the attempt count must not reset the clock. The walk is global rather than per provider because the chain it cuts belongs to the request, a combo, its accounts and their keys.

total_ms.description: The wall clock one request's failover walk may spend, in milliseconds. Unset keeps the stored value. The default is 30000, the ceiling a single transport call already gets (SPEC-API-001 §7.7 and §7.14).

max_attempts.description: How many credentials one request may spend before the walk reports what it already learned. The default is 8.

ProviderStrategyPatch.description: One provider's override. An entry must set at least one field; deleting the entry is how a provider returns to the global default.

failure_classes.description: This provider's per-class overrides, merged over the group's. An absent class inherits.

provider_thinking.description: Per-provider thinking modes, keyed by provider id. Sent whole; deleting an entry is how a provider returns to the client's own reasoning intent.

ProviderThinkingPatch.description: One provider's stored reasoning mode. "auto" is not a value; deleting the entry is how a provider returns to the client's own reasoning intent.

provider_proxies.description: Per-provider proxy bindings, keyed by provider id. Sent whole; an absent entry inherits the global setting, `__none__` dials direct, and any other pool_id names a stored proxy row to try first.

ProviderProxyPatch.description: One provider's proxy binding. An entry must set at least one field; deleting the entry is how a provider returns to the global setting.

ProviderStatusSummary.description: Endpoint counts per state for one provider.

auth_hint.description: The registry's credential-format sentence (draft 036 slice B), served verbatim, and it names the upstream URL where the operator mints the credential. Absent when the provider declares none.

BulkResultRow.description: One row's outcome inside a batch answer. A row that refused for its own reason carries the code beside the message, so a client maps one conflicted credential without reading prose.

BulkSelector.description: The rows one bulk action addresses (SPEC-API-001 §7.5). Exactly one of ids, tag or all names a set: nothing named is a refusal rather than everything, and two named is a refusal rather than an intersection. provider_id and auth_type narrow whichever form is set, and all with no provider spans every provider, native and custom alike. The set is resolved in storage, never in a browser.

BulkStatusRequest.description: Park or release every row a selector resolves to. An omitted window_hours takes the provider's own reset cadence, so a disabled account returns to rotation by the clock rather than by a job.

BulkDeleteRequest.description: Remove every row a selector resolves to, in one transaction.

BulkTagsRequest.description: Add, remove, or clear tags across the resolved set. add and remove may both be filled in one call because retagging a set is one intent.

BulkProxyStatusRequest.description: Switch every candidate a selector resolves to on or off. A candidate that carries no tag, provider, or auth type refuses a selector that narrows by one, rather than acting on the whole pool and calling it the subset.

BulkProxyDeleteRequest.description: Erase every candidate a selector resolves to. confirm_endpoints is the number of connections the operator saw lose their egress path; the server counts them from storage and refuses when the two differ.

ProxyPinsResponse.description: What a bulk erase took down with it.

BulkProxyResponse.description: What a proxy bulk action did, with the pin report beside the row results.

BulkMutationResponse.description: What a bulk mutation did. matched is the server's own count of the resolved set rather than the rows one page showed, so the panel reports what the action covered.

thinking_levels.description: Levels this model accepts when appended to its name (SPEC-API-001 §7.14). Absent when the registry knows no levels for it.
Levels this model accepts when appended to its name (SPEC-API-001 §7.14). Absent when the registry knows no levels for it.

latency_ms.description: Sum of every matched request's own duration in milliseconds, so it grows with the request count. latency_p50_ms and latency_p95_ms carry the per-request picture.

latency_p50_ms.description: Median latency over the matched requests, in milliseconds.

latency_p95_ms.description: 95th percentile latency over the matched requests, in milliseconds.

latency_ms.description: This request's own duration in milliseconds. Unlike UsageTotals.latency_ms, which sums a window, this field measures one call.

fallback_strategy.description: The effective global default, never an empty string.

provider_strategies.description: The stored overrides, rendered as {} rather than null when there are none.

failure_classes.description: The stored per-class overrides, not the effective table. A class with no entry is absent, because the documented default is the build's answer rather than something an operator decided.

FailureClassPolicyResponse.description: One stored class override, in the units the wire carries. Fields an entry leaves unset are absent, so the panel renders what was decided rather than a filled-in copy.

KeyParkResponse.description: The effective key-parking budget in seconds (SPEC-API-001 §7.5). The group answers what the router will actually use, so a document that predates the keys still names 120, 2, 900 and 30 rather than blanks.

FailoverBudgetResponse.description: The effective credential-walk budget the router applies (SPEC-API-001 §7.14). Both bounds are always named, so a document stored before the keys existed answers 30000 and 8 rather than the zeros an operator would read as no walk allowed.

total_ms.description: The milliseconds one request's credential walk may spend, as the router applies it.

max_attempts.description: The credentials one request may spend before the walk reports what it already learned, as the router applies it.

ProviderStrategyResponse.description: One provider's stored override. An absent field inherits the global default, so the panel renders what is stored rather than a filled-in copy.

failure_classes.description: The classes this provider's entry overrides, and only those.

provider_thinking.description: The stored modes, rendered as {} rather than null when there are none.

ProviderThinkingResponse.description: One provider's stored reasoning mode. An absent entry is the "auto" state, so the panel renders the mode it reads rather than a filled-in copy.

provider_proxies.description: The stored bindings, rendered as {} rather than null when there are none.

ProviderProxyResponse.description: One provider's stored binding. An absent field inherits the global setting, so the panel renders what is stored rather than a filled-in copy.

refresh_retry_at.description: When the worker will next attempt this account's refresh grant. Absent on a live account: the ladder only speaks for an account the vendor has already refused five times (SPEC-API-001 §7.4, draft 050 T2).

refresh_retry_rounds.description: How many times the account has been buried without a grant succeeding, which is the step its next window was taken from.

skipped.description: The accounts a provider-wide sweep passed over, each with its reason. Refreshing one named endpoint answers its refusal as an error instead, so this is empty on that path.

endpoint_id.description: The account the sweep left alone.

reason.description: The refusal that account received, in the same English client-facing text the error would have produced on its own.

device_code.description: The single-use handle every poll of this round carries back.

verification_url.description: The vendor's device page, shown as a link the operator opens. The panel never fetches it.

user_code.description: The short code the operator recognizes. Display only; the vendor does not read it. Present only when the round's flow mints one; a vendor-minted state round has no short code and omits the key.

status.description: pending means the operator has not finished the vendor page yet and the caller keeps polling at the start's interval.

endpoint_id.description: Present only when connected, and it names the upstream endpoint the flow landed.

token_hint.description: The masked credential hint of the connected account. The token itself never crosses this boundary.

created.description: True when this login created the endpoint, false when it refreshed a known account onto it.

SystemOneRequest.description: The body of POST /api/v1/systemone (§7.15). State is the situation to evaluate and Questions is the map of decisions to ask about it, keyed by the caller's own name for each question. Both are required; the inner shape of each travels verbatim because it belongs to the upstream, not the gateway.

SystemOneUsage.description: The token accounting a decision answer reports.

SystemOneAnswer.description: The decision endpoint's own answer, forwarded as the upstream wrote it. The gateway reads only usage for accounting; the rest of the shape is the provider's vocabulary and reaches the client untouched.

error.message: The request is invalid.

ManagementForbiddenError.description: The session is valid but the operation is not permitted.

ManagementNotFoundError.description: The addressed resource does not exist.

error.message: The requested resource was not found.

ManagementMethodNotAllowedError.description: The method is not registered for this path.

error.message: The method is not allowed for this route.

ManagementConflictError.description: The request conflicts with stored state or a uniqueness constraint.

error.message: The request conflicts with existing state.

BulkCountMismatchError.description: The set a bulk action resolved to is not the set the caller confirmed, so the action was refused and nothing was written.

error.message: The selector now resolves to a different number of rows than this action confirmed.

BulkTargetTooLargeError.description: The selector resolves past the ceiling one bulk action may address, and the refusal names the count it resolved to so the caller knows how far to narrow.

error.message: This selector resolves to more rows than one action may address.

ManagementRateLimitedError.description: The caller exceeded a configured rate limit.

error.message: Too many requests. Try again later.

ManagementUpstreamError.description: An upstream provider returned an unrecoverable error.

error.message: The upstream request failed.

ManagementUnavailableError.description: No provider or endpoint can serve the request.

error.message: No provider is available for this request.

ManagementTimeoutError.description: An upstream call exceeded its deadline.

error.message: The upstream request timed out.

ManagementInternalError.description: An unexpected error occurred; the request id in the log names the cause.

error.message: An unexpected error occurred.

DataPlaneBadRequestError.description: The request is invalid: it failed schema validation, or named a provider the gateway cannot translate, or the upstream refused the request itself (draft 042 R11: the refusal is the wire's 400 invalid_request_error, not a 502 outage).

error.message: The request is invalid.
The provider cannot be reached through this gateway.

DataPlaneNotFoundError.description: The model string resolved to nothing: no combo, no alias, and no provider the registry knows. SPEC-API-001 §7.15 ends the resolution order here, and the status matches the OpenAI wire, which answers a model it does not know with 404 invalid_request_error.

get.summary: Live stream of what the gateway is routing now
get.description:
Server-sent events. Each frame is full state for the three facts a period window cannot carry:
the requests in flight now, the requests that just finished, and the provider the gateway last
reported an error for. A frame is sent when that state changes, and an idle connection receives
an SSE comment (`: ping`) rather than a frame, so a client counting frames is never told a change
happened. The status line and the SSE headers are committed with the first frame, so a failure
before it is an ordinary HTTP error in the management envelope.

200.description: An SSE stream of live frames.

get.summary: The provider's own quota for one endpoint
get.description:
The connection's published allocation, served from the cache the poll
worker writes, as opposed to GET /api/v1/quotas/{endpoint_id}, which
reports the windows this gateway counted. The two answers disagree by
nature and neither corrects the other, so they are separate bodies.

`?force=1` asks the provider for this one account at this instant
instead of reading the cache. It is the operator's explicit press on a
single card (the same seam the reference's per-card refresh uses) and
the reason the screen itself never has to fan out. A value other than
`1` is a cache read, so a stale bookmark or a rewriting proxy cannot
turn a page load into provider traffic.

A provider that publishes no usage endpoint, or an endpoint with no
stored credential, is refused; a provider that answers with an error or
nothing at all is a 200 with `message` and an empty `data`.

parameters.name: force
parameters.description: `"1"` asks the provider now rather than reading the worker's cache. Any other value is a cache read.
